title: Paul Ginsparg and the Founding of arXiv (1991)
explainer: Before arXiv, a researcher tracking the frontier had to wait months for journal publication or hope to be on the right mailing list; Paul Ginsparg built arXiv at Los Alamos in 1991 as a central repository so physicists could share typeset preprints instantly instead of flooding each other's inboxes. That norm of posting work publicly before (or instead of) formal peer review is exactly why a modern independent research agenda in ML is even possible: nearly every major result you'll track down - from optimizer tricks to new architectures - appears on arXiv first, often years before any conference version. Understanding where this preprint culture came from clarifies why 'frontier tracking' in ML means reading arXiv listings and citation graphs, not waiting for textbooks.
